## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Mettābhāvanā Sutta* ("The Meditation on Love", Iti 27; PTS It 19) is a discourse preserved in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, the Buddha teaches that goodwill far outshines all other ways of making merit, declaring that whatever grounds for making worldly merit exist (*opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni*), none match even a sixteenth part of the mind-deliverance of loving-kindness (*mettā cetovimutti*) [SuttaCentral; SI TI LA 2014].

SuttaCentral identifies a full Chinese parallel to the sutta at T 765.50 (修慈), a passage-level parallel in the *Aṭṭhakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 8.1 *Mettāsutta*), and a resembling parallel in the *Cakkavākajātaka* (Ja 451) [SuttaCentral]. The discourse is also mentioned in post-canonical treatises, specifically the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 3) and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.6.2) [SuttaCentral]. 

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms close links with AN 8, finding a large shared passage between Iti 27 (§6.1–10.4) and AN 8.1 (§1.2.4–1.7.4) [DharmaNexus]. In total, DharmaNexus identifies 209 matching passages across 20 Pali texts, with significant shared material in the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2), *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Cūḷasakuludāyi Sutta* (MN 79), and the commentary *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Tibetan canonical texts, scoring highest with the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D4099) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral indexes 19 modern translations of the sutta in 16 languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
